title: Facebook leads — Oct 24, 2026 all-goods review
summary_md:
This review covers **everything the Facebook watcher has collected so far**: 11,997 listings, including a new sweep on Oct 23–24 that added clothing & shoes, kids & baby, home & kitchen, and books/movies/music. **7,047 were local** (within 60 mi of Keller, still available, not services or food). Every one was looked at photo-by-photo under the Facebook rules — now covering **all kinds of goods and anything brand-name**, not mainly cards and collectibles.

**Result: 102 leads** — 5 Tier A, 68 Tier B, 29 Tier C. **72 are new**; 30 were also in the Oct 23 report (marked in their price note) and are kept here so this report stands on its own.

**Act first on Tier A**, closest first. Free and $0/$1 listings are common; the $1 is usually a placeholder, so ask the real price before driving.

**Caveats:** most of these were posted Oct 21–24, and good Facebook posts often go within a day, so message before you drive. The sold-price checkers ran out of search budget partway and eBay's sold pages were blocked, so **most values are conservative estimates**, not confirmed sold comps. Each lead says which. Treat Tier C as "worth a message", not "worth a trip".
howto_md:
1. **Filter and sort** with the bar above the list (it remembers your choices). *Sort: recommended* = Tier A first, biggest margin first. Filter by category to see just clothing, kitchen, books and so on.
2. **Open a lead** (Details): what it is, why it's worth it, where to resell, the main risk, a checklist, a ready-to-copy **message to the seller**, and an **offer plan** (open at / walk away at).
3. **Message the seller** from Facebook (button on each lead). Ask the question in the message first, because many prices are placeholders ($0/$1) or per-item.
4. **Set the status** on the lead page as you go (Messaged → Offer made → Bought, or Passed / gone), and add **notes** for seller replies and pickup times. If the site's database is paused, statuses and notes won't save, but the report still loads.
5. **Never pay above the max offer.** Free items: just confirm and pick up.
method_md:
- **Collected:** Refurbish Watcher sweeps on Oct 23–24, 2026: antiques, jewelry, instruments, hobbies, free, toys, entertainment, sports, home improvement, **plus clothing & shoes, family/kids & baby, home & kitchen, and books/movies/music** (local pickup, ≤ 50 mi of Keller, newest first). 11,997 listings in total.
- **Screened:** all 7,047 local listings' main photos, 25 per sheet at large size, under the updated Facebook brief: judge the photo, not the title; the listed price is a ceiling; cover clothing, kids' toys and baby gear, books, kitchen and home, tools and anything brand-name as well as collectibles. Flag if resale minus a realistic offer is ≥ $50 and resale is ≥ 3× the price. That gave 451 flags.
- **Checked:** each flag went to a second agent that looked at the photo again and tried to find sold prices, keeping only items that clear the rule. Pianos, organs, heavy multi-person items under $500, replicas and dealer ads were killed. Each kept lead was then written up from its photo and the checker's notes.
- **Limits:** one photo per listing (descriptions and extra photos weren't read, so open the listing). Values are mostly estimates (see each lead). Distances are from the listing's city to Keller.
